title: Sentry Dashboard: GPU Pool Health, Autoscale & Burst Rules Prototype
creator: Jonah Patel
description: Design and prototype a consolidated 'Sentry' dashboard for Dedicated GPU pools that combines health overview, autoscaling controls, burst rule authoring, and cost overlays. This ticket covers exploratory screens, an interactive Figma prototype for user testing, handoff artifacts for front-end engineering, and a review cycle with PM/Eng to finalize behavior and edge cases.
background: Operators currently bounce between multiple views (pool list, low-level metrics, and an autoscale policy editor). Support teams and customers need a single surface for quick triage, controlled burst activation, and cost visibility. The design should reduce time to action when pools show elevated latency or running cost spikes.
goals: Create a single glanceable health summary for each GPU pool with signal prioritization
Provide an inline autoscale policy editor with safe defaults and previewed effects
Support a reusable burst-rule composer: rule templates, conditional triggers, and one-click apply
Surface cost impact of autoscale/burst decisions via a sparkline and per-minute cost delta
Enable canary and rollback controls for rollout of autoscale/burst changes
proposed_design_components: Top-line health strip: status chip, SLO breach badge, 3 key metrics (p99 latency, throughput, utilization)
Temporal sparkline row: latency, queue length, and estimated cost overlay with adjustable horizon
Autoscale editor pane: min/max, scale step, cooldown slider, estimated concurrency curve preview
Burst Composer modal: trigger selector (metric threshold, schedule, manual), duration, budget cap, template gallery
Cost impact preview: delta bar with conservative/expected/optimistic bands
Rollouts control bar: canary percentage, rollout duration, automatic rollback toggle, audit log link
prototypes: Clickable flows: health-triage -> compose burst -> simulate cost -> confirm apply
decisions: Show cost overlay by default but collapse to reduce noise; expand on hover or via 'show cost' toggle
Burst rules must support a budget cap to prevent runaway spend
Autoscale preview uses historical 24h workload to estimate steady-state cost and peak impact
Canary rollouts default to 10% for customer-facing pools, configurable per-pool
tradeoffs: Surface more signals vs visual complexity: chose a minimal 3-metric summary to keep the primary strip compact
In-dashboard rule authoring speeds ops but increases UI surface area; mitigated by templates and guided defaults
Estimating cost is heuristic and may mislead; included conservative/expected/optimistic bands and clear tooltip language
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates full compose/apply/cancel flow for burst rules with cost preview
Design tokens and component variants ready for engineering handoff (states, spacing, responsive rules)
PM and Eng signoff on autoscale constraints (min/max, cooldown, step) and canary default
Usability test with at least 5 platform engineers with tasks: triage a degraded pool, create a time-bound burst, and interpret cost preview
Audit log entry shape and metadata defined and documented for backend consumption
review_comments: PM (Rafael Ortiz): Request to show expected request queue depth after applying autoscale policy
SRE (Amira Khan): Add explicit emergency 'drain and scale down' action for noisy tenants
Eng lead (Noah Green): Front-end complexity concern around live sparkline overlays; propose offloading simulation to a backend endpoint
Design reviewer (Maya Chen): Suggest stronger microcopy for budget cap tooltip to avoid accidental overspend
next_steps: Incorporate review feedback and update prototype by 2026-03-14
Run 1:1 usability sessions with 6 internal users between 2026-03-15 and 2026-03-18
Finalize component spec and create engineering tickets by 2026-03-20
Coordinate with Eng to expose cost-sim endpoint and audit-log schema
